summary: The change is well contained: one warning that never stops a launch, placed beside the #16 warning, with a spec that says plainly what was and was not probed. The two correctness findings are about the warning's advice and timing: on a resume it arrives too late to act on, and it offers bypass-permissions without saying that this removes the coverage pass's stated safety. The rest are wording and record-keeping that drifted from the branch. The Docs and Version checks pass (`docs/running.md` is named in the plan; `shape.md` keeps 0.2.0 on purpose), and no scheduled or queued work touches these prompt and doc files.

findings.title: The inserted sentences change what "reviewed without it" refers to
findings.description: The two sentences added before "The launch precheck warns when this repository is reviewed without it" separate "it" from `--plugin-dir`. The nearest candidates are now "An installed release" and "bypass-permissions". Read that way, the precheck warns when this repository is reviewed without an installed release, which is the opposite of the #16 warning: that one fires when the session is not on `--plugin-dir`.
findings.proposedFix: Say "reviewed without `--plugin-dir`" in that sentence, or move the new sentences after it.

findings.title: plan.md's As built is stale against the branch and the PR body
findings.description: Gate step 13 requires `plan.md` to reflect what was built. As built still says "Task 3 waits for the PR number" (line 87), but commit 00b04f3 added the `#83` CHANGELOG line. It also says "Not walked yet: the inline session" (line 91), while the PR body says the inline walk was done. Shape decision 8 makes that walk a condition of the merge, so the spec's record cannot show it was met.
findings.proposedFix: Update As built: Task 3 landed in 00b04f3, and the inline walk was done with `/redline:redline 80 dry run review only`, showing the warning at precheck step 1 and stopping at the branch check. Keep the resume path and the installed-release session as not walked.

findings.title: The approved standards edit did not land in its own commit
findings.description: CLAUDE.md and gate step 12.4 require approved standards edits in their own commit, separate from the spec's code. `git show --stat 4edbbb7` lists `release.md` together with `skills/redline/SKILL.md`, `docs/running.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the spec folder, and the PR has only that commit and the CHANGELOG one. `plan.md` ("on its own", and As built "Built as shaped, with no deviation") and `shape.md` line 33 ("in its own commit") state something the history does not show. Merges here keep their commits (#80 is a merge commit), so the lump stays on `main`.
findings.proposedFix: Question for the person: split 4edbbb7 by hand before the merge so the standards bullet stands alone (a Redline run cannot rewrite history), or keep the history and record the deviation under Decisions in `shape.md` and in As built, correcting the "in its own commit" line.

findings.title: The resume warning comes after the person's last chance to act on it
findings.description: On a resume the paragraph is said after the Resume/Start fresh `AskUserQuestion` (line 47) and after `run check` exits 0. For an `error` or `stopped` marker the relaunch follows in the same turn (lines 50, 52, 53: nothing else is typed first). Earlier agents replay from cache in seconds, so for the case shape decision 6 names, an error at `post r<n>` in auto mode, the post reruns at once and is refused again. The person sees the warning but has no pause in which to change the mode, and has to resume a second time. Decision 6 justifies the resume warning by exactly this person ("would hit the same refusal unwarned").
findings.proposedFix: Say the Inline session paragraph, under its condition, before the Resume/Start fresh question on line 47 (or inside the question), so the answer can follow a change of mode. Remove it from the exit-0 sequence.

findings.title: The hand-off exemption inside the Resume bullet contradicts it for `handoff` and `reviewed` markers
findings.description: The bullet says to say the paragraph on a resume, then adds "a relaunch after a hand-off does not repeat it". A section 7 relaunch never comes through this bullet, and section 4 already opens "Precheck (fresh launches only)" and skips it on a relaunch after a hand-off. Inside the bullet, then, the clause can only read as an exception for this bullet's own `handoff` marker, whose sub-bullet says "relaunch". A person who reopens the session with `claude --resume <id>` and resumes such a marker gets no warning, while `docs/running.md` promises one "on a resume", and shape decision 6's reason for silence ("same session, already said") is about the in-session relaunch.
findings.proposedFix: Delete the clause; section 4's heading already keeps a section 7 relaunch silent. If it stays, say "a section 7 relaunch in the same session does not repeat it".

findings.title: The warning recommends bypass-permissions without saying it removes the coverage pass's stated safety
findings.description: README Known limits (line 101) and `agent-os/standards/scripts/guard.md` line 23 say the code-review fork carries no Redline `agent_type`, that its safety is the skill's read-only recipe and the session's permission mode, and that a `redline-gh.sh` write from the fork is inert to the guard so the session's permission prompt decides (#80, R2-5). The new warning, and the matching sentences in `docs/running.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`, offer bypass-permissions as an equal remedy with no caveat. In bypass-permissions that prompt does not exist, so a fork that posts, replies or resolves threads, for example steered by text in the PR under review, goes through unasked. This PR is the first place Redline tells a person to use that mode, and it does so on the self-review path.
findings.proposedFix: Question for the person: keep bypass-permissions in the warning with one clause stating the cost (the coverage pass then runs with no permission prompt; `coverage off` avoids that), or drop it and name only accept-edits, accepting that a headless inline session then has no stated remedy. Whichever is chosen, the same wording goes in `docs/running.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and the README's Known limits bullet.

forThePerson.text: The bypass-permissions remedy is not part of the recorded probe, which covered auto and accept-edits; nothing on file shows a subagent Write passing under `--plugin-dir` in bypass, so one real session would confirm it.

The condition also fires for the local-directory marketplace, which the probe did not cover; there the warning's flat claim about auto mode is untested, and it asks the person to give up auto mode, so "costs a line" may understate it.
The bullet says one launcher Write was refused where `shape.md` says refused twice, and "in either mode", following a both-launches comparison, can read as covering plain `claude`.

The header and gate step 11 say the entry is written by the person at tag time from merged PR titles; #80 set the same early-entry precedent and this line differs from the PR title, so either the rule or the practice could change.

A one-line subagent Write probe at launch could detect the refusal directly, avoiding the false alarm in accept-edits and bypass and the roughly 23-minute loss before `post r<n>` in auto mode; a larger design than this PR chose.

The inline test and its verbatim paragraph live only in prompt prose that no test reads; an `inline` field from `redline-setup.sh version` and `redline-prefs.sh run check` would put them under the script tests, which decision 1 excluded for this PR.

Already tracked in #76, which lacks this: once #76 closes after the installed-release walk, the unfiled upstream report has no open home, and nothing says when to remove the warning after Claude Code fixes the refusal.

accounting.ref: The warning already names bypass-permissions, the option that applies in a headless session, so the remedy can be followed there.

Needs a Windows path, a relocated seed cache with no plugins parent, or a --plugin-dir checkout under a /plugins/cache/ path; the outcome is one warning line more or fewer, and the launch never stops on it.
